1: # Trellis Requirements
2: 
3: This document defines the requirements for Trellis, the `verified-logic` Rust library.
4: Every requirement has a Tracey ID and maps to verified Rust code.
5: 
6: ## Bitwise
7: 
8: r[bitwise.is-power-of-two]
9: is_power_of_two MUST return true if and only if the value is a power of two
10: (exactly one bit set). Zero MUST return false.
11: 
12: r[bitwise.bit-at]
13: bit_at MUST return true if and only if the bit at the given position is set.
14: Position MUST be in the range [0, 64).
15: 
16: r[bitwise.set-bit]
17: set_bit MUST return a value with the bit at the given position set to 1,
18: leaving all other bits unchanged.
19: 
20: r[bitwise.clear-bit]
21: clear_bit MUST return a value with the bit at the given position set to 0,
22: leaving all other bits unchanged.
23: 
24: r[bitwise.toggle-bit]
25: toggle_bit MUST return a value with the bit at the given position flipped.
26: Toggling twice MUST return the original value.
27: 
28: r[bitwise.is-sign-extended]
29: is_sign_extended(value, width) MUST return true if and only if bits [63:width]
30: of value are all copies of bit [width-1]. width MUST be in [1, 64].
31: is_sign_extended(value, 64) MUST always return true. If
32: is_sign_extended(value, w1) holds and w2 >= w1, then
33: is_sign_extended(value, w2) MUST also hold.
34: 
35: ## Arithmetic
36: 
37: r[arithmetic.abs-diff]
38: The absolute difference function MUST return |a - b| for any two unsigned
39: integers without overflow.
40: 
41: r[arithmetic.saturating-add]
42: Saturating addition MUST return a + b clamped to the maximum value of the
43: type, never wrapping.
44: 
45: r[arithmetic.saturating-sub]
46: Saturating subtraction MUST return a - b clamped to zero when b > a,
47: never wrapping.
48: 
49: r[arithmetic.checked-mul]
50: Checked multiplication MUST return None when the result would overflow
51: the type's range, and Some(a * b) otherwise.
52: 
53: r[arithmetic.gcd]
54: The greatest common divisor function MUST compute the GCD via the Euclidean
55: algorithm. gcd(a, 0) MUST return a. gcd(0, a) MUST return a.
56: 
57: r[arithmetic.div-ceil]
58: Ceiling division MUST return the smallest integer >= a/b. div_ceil(0, b)
59: MUST return 0. The divisor MUST be nonzero.
60: 
61: ## Bounds
62: 
63: r[bounds.in-range]
64: The in-range predicate MUST return true if and only if the value is
65: within the inclusive range [lo, hi].
66: 
67: r[bounds.clamp]
68: Clamp MUST return lo when value < lo, hi when value > hi, and value
69: otherwise. The result MUST always satisfy in-range(result, lo, hi).
70: 
71: ## Collections
72: 
73: r[collections.sorted-insert]
74: Inserting into a sorted sequence MUST produce a sorted sequence containing
75: all original elements plus the new element.
76: 
77: r[collections.binary-search]
78: Binary search on a sorted sequence MUST return the index of the target if
79: present, or None if absent. It MUST NOT access indices outside the sequence
80: bounds.
81: 
82: r[collections.merge-sorted]
83: Merging two sorted sequences MUST produce a sorted sequence whose length
84: equals the sum of the input lengths.
85: 
86: r[collections.is-partitioned]
87: is_partitioned MUST return true if and only if all elements below the
88: threshold precede all elements at or above it. Sorted sequences MUST be
89: partitioned by any threshold. Empty slices MUST be partitioned.
90: 
91: r[collections.find-first]
92: find_first MUST return the index of the first occurrence of target, or
93: None if absent. When found, no earlier index may contain the target.
94: find_first on an empty slice MUST return None.
95: 
96: r[collections.count-matches]
97: count_matches MUST return the number of elements equal to target. The
98: count MUST be zero for empty slices. The count MUST never exceed the
99: slice length.
100: 
101: ## Integer
102: 
103: r[integer.is-even]
104: is_even MUST return true if and only if x is divisible by 2. is_even and
105: is_odd MUST be complements: exactly one is true for any input.
106: 
107: r[integer.is-odd]
108: is_odd MUST return true if and only if x is not divisible by 2.
109: 
110: r[integer.align-down]
111: align_down MUST return the largest multiple of `align` that is <= x. The
112: result MUST be <= x. The result MUST be divisible by `align`. Alignment 1
113: MUST be the identity function.
114: 
115: r[integer.align-up]
116: align_up MUST return the smallest multiple of `align` that is >= x, or
117: None if the result would overflow u64. When defined, the result MUST be
118: >= x and divisible by `align`. Alignment 1 MUST be the identity.
119: 
120: r[integer.log2-floor]
121: log2_floor MUST return floor(log2(x)) for x > 0. log2_floor(1) MUST be 0.
122: log2_floor(2) MUST be 1.
123: 
124: r[integer.next-power-of-two]
125: next_power_of_two MUST return the smallest power of 2 >= x, or None on
126: overflow. next_power_of_two(0) and next_power_of_two(1) MUST return
127: Some(1).
128: 
129: ## Ordering
130: 
131: r[ordering.min]
132: min MUST return the smaller of two values. min MUST be commutative,
133: associative, and idempotent.
134: 
135: r[ordering.max]
136: max MUST return the larger of two values. max MUST be commutative,
137: associative, and idempotent. min(a, b) <= max(a, b) MUST hold.
138: 
139: r[ordering.median-of-three]
140: median_of_three MUST return the middle value of three inputs. The result
141: MUST be bounded by the overall min and max of the three values. The median
142: of three equal values MUST be that value.
143: 
144: r[ordering.sign]
145: sign MUST return -1 if a < b, 0 if a == b, and 1 if a > b.
146: sign MUST be antisymmetric: sign(a, b) == -sign(b, a).
147: 
148: r[ordering.compare-and-swap]
149: compare_and_swap MUST return (min(a,b), max(a,b)). The first element MUST
150: be less than or equal to the second. Both input values MUST be preserved.
151: 
152: ## Cross-Module Properties
153: 
154: r[properties.abs-diff-zero-iff-equal]
155: abs_diff(a, b) MUST equal zero if and only if a equals b.
156: 
157: r[properties.add-sub-roundtrip]
158: When a + b does not overflow, saturating_sub(saturating_add(a, b), b) MUST
159: return a. Addition and subtraction MUST be inverse operations within bounds.
160: 
161: r[properties.triangle-inequality]
162: abs_diff MUST satisfy the triangle inequality: abs_diff(a, c) is less than
163: or equal to abs_diff(a, b) + abs_diff(b, c) for all a, b, c.
164: 
165: r[properties.clamp-nearest-point]
166: For any x in [lo, hi], clamp(value, lo, hi) MUST be at least as close to
167: value as x is. Clamp returns the nearest point in the range.
168: 
169: r[properties.clamp-monotonic]
170: Clamp MUST be monotonic: if a <= b then clamp(a, lo, hi) <= clamp(b, lo, hi).
171: 
172: r[properties.distance-decomposition]
173: For any value in [lo, hi], the distances to the endpoints MUST sum to the
174: range width: abs_diff(value, lo) + abs_diff(value, hi) == abs_diff(lo, hi).
175: 
176: r[properties.sub-add-inverse]
177: When b <= a, saturating_add(saturating_sub(a, b), b) MUST return a.
178: Subtraction and addition MUST be inverse operations within bounds.
179: 
180: r[properties.set-clear-roundtrip]
181: Setting a bit then clearing it MUST leave the bit cleared. Clearing a bit
182: then setting it MUST leave the bit set. set_bit and clear_bit MUST be
183: complementary operations on individual bit positions.
184: 
185: r[properties.toggle-involution]
186: Toggling a bit twice MUST return the original value for any input and
187: any valid bit position.
188: 
189: r[properties.min-max-abs-diff]
190: max(a, b) - min(a, b) MUST equal abs_diff(a, b). The gap between min and
191: max is the absolute difference.
192: 
193: r[properties.clamp-via-min-max]
194: clamp(v, lo, hi) MUST equal min(max(v, lo), hi) when lo <= hi. Clamp is
195: expressible as nested min/max.
196: 
197: r[properties.align-down-remainder]
198: x - align_down(x, a) MUST equal x % a. The distance from x to the
199: aligned-down value is the remainder.
200: 
201: r[properties.align-up-via-div-ceil]
202: When align_up(x, a) is defined, it MUST equal div_ceil(x, a) * a. Rounding
203: up to an alignment is ceiling division times the alignment.
204: 
205: r[properties.median-is-clamp]
206: median_of_three(a, b, c) MUST equal clamp(a, min(b, c), max(b, c)).
207: The median is a clamped value.
208: 
209: r[properties.all-equal-implies-count]
210: If all_equal(s, v) holds, count_matches(s, v) MUST equal s.len(). Every
211: element matching means the count is the full length.
212: 
213: r[properties.chunk-count-div-ceil]
214: div_ceil(n, k) MUST equal chunk_count(n, k) + 1 when n has a remainder
215: mod k, and chunk_count(n, k) when it divides evenly. Floor and ceiling
216: division differ by exactly the presence of a remainder.
217: 
218: r[properties.narrow-iff-in-range]
219: narrow_u32(x).is_some() MUST hold if and only if in_range(x, 0, u32::MAX)
220: holds. Checked narrowing and range predicates MUST agree.
221: 
222: r[properties.all-equal-implies-partitioned]
223: If all_equal(s, v) holds, is_partitioned(s, threshold) MUST hold for any
224: threshold. A uniform sequence is trivially partitioned.
225: 
226: r[properties.majority-via-div-ceil]
227: majority(n) MUST equal div_ceil(n + 1, 2) for all n > 0. The majority
228: threshold is ceiling division of (n+1) by 2.
229: 
230: r[properties.epoch-ge-term-index]
231: epoch_ge(a, b) MUST imply a.term > b.term, or a.term == b.term and
232: a.index >= b.index. The lexicographic comparison decomposes into term
233: and index conditions.
234: 
235: r[properties.log-prefix-term-eq]
236: If logs_match_prefix(a, b, k) holds, the term sequences of a and b
237: MUST be equal over [0, k). Log term-agreement is equivalent to prefix
238: equality on the projected term sequence.
239: 
240: r[properties.chaoscontrol-subset-replay]
241: For normalized schedules, if `subset(source, indices)` is replayed from
242: `cursor = 0` by any nondecreasing time sequence whose final horizon covers all
243: subset faults, delivered faults MUST appear in the same relative order as in
244: `source`.
245: 
246: r[properties.chaoscontrol-fingerprint-trace]
247: For schedulers that start from the same initial state, or the same full
248: post-`apply_variant` reset state, executions with the same post-advance
249: turn/quantum trace MUST produce the same fingerprint even if the imperative
250: shell path differs.
251: 
252: r[properties.chaoscontrol-quorum-gate]
253: For valid fault states, a healthy-period gate MUST never report healthy unless
254: the corresponding `quorum_reachable` predicate holds for that same state.
255: 
256: ## Consistency Model Vocabulary
257: 
258: r[consistency-vocab.valid-op-kind]
259: The shared consistency-history vocabulary MUST use four operation tags:
260: read, write, commit, and abort. Any other tag MUST be rejected.
261: 
262: r[consistency-vocab.op-complete]
263: A shared history operation MUST be complete when it has a valid tag and
264: its invocation time is less than or equal to its response time.
265: 
266: r[consistency-vocab.same-object]
267: Two history operations MUST be considered on the same object if and only
268: if their object identifiers are equal.
269: 
270: r[consistency-vocab.same-transaction]
271: Two history operations MUST be considered in the same transaction if and
272: only if their transaction identifiers are equal.
273: 
274: r[consistency-vocab.same-session]
275: Two history operations MUST be considered in the same session if and only
276: if their session identifiers are equal.
277: 
278: ## Shamir Secret Sharing
279: 
280: r[shamir-field.prime-modulus]
281: Shamir field arithmetic MUST validate that the modulus is prime and less
282: than 2^32. Composite moduli MUST be rejected.
283: 
284: r[shamir-field.closure]
285: Field addition and multiplication modulo p MUST return values in [0, p).
286: The modulus MUST satisfy 1 < p < 2^32 and be prime.
287: 
288: r[shamir-field.additive-identity]
289: Zero MUST be the additive identity: a + 0 == a and 0 + a == a.
290: 
291: r[shamir-field.multiplicative-identity]
292: One MUST be the multiplicative identity: a * 1 == a and 1 * a == a.
293: 
294: r[shamir-field.commutativity]
295: Field addition and multiplication MUST be commutative.
296: 
297: r[shamir-field.multiplicative-inverse]
298: Any inverse returned for a non-zero element MUST multiply back to one.
299: Zero MUST have no inverse.
300: 
301: r[shamir-field.subtraction]
302: Field subtraction MUST satisfy (a - b) + b == a modulo p.
303: 
304: r[shamir-poly.horner-correctness]
305: Polynomial evaluation by Horner's method MUST match the recursive
306: polynomial sum definition. Evaluating at zero MUST return the constant term.
307: 
308: r[shamir-poly.degree-bound]
309: A polynomial with k coefficients MUST have degree at most k - 1.
310: 
311: r[shamir-lagrange.kronecker-delta]
312: The i-th Lagrange basis function MUST equal 1 at x_i and 0 at x_j for j != i.
313: 
314: r[shamir-lagrange.partition-of-unity]
315: The Lagrange basis values at any interpolation point MUST sum to 1.
316: 
317: r[shamir-lagrange.interpolation-correctness]
318: The Lagrange interpolant MUST reproduce the provided y-values at the
319: interpolation points. Evaluating it at zero MUST support reconstruction.
320: 
321: r[shamir-lagrange.uniqueness]
322: A value vector over fixed distinct interpolation points MUST be uniquely
323: determined by its interpolated values on those points.
324: 
325: r[shamir-split.share-count]
326: Split MUST return exactly one share per requested x-coordinate and preserve
327: those x-coordinates in the output.
328: 
329: r[shamir-split.parameter-validation]
330: Split MUST reject degenerate thresholds and invalid x-coordinates.
331: Threshold MUST satisfy 2 <= k <= n.
332: 
333: r[shamir-split.constant-term-preservation]
334: The secret MUST be the constant term of the split polynomial. Evaluating the
335: polynomial at x = 0 MUST return the secret.
336: 
337: r[shamir-reconstruct.correctness]
338: Reconstruction from k valid shares MUST return the secret encoded by the
339: threshold polynomial used to generate those shares.
340: 
341: r[shamir-reconstruct.insufficient-shares]
342: Reconstruction from fewer than k shares SHOULD NOT recover the original
343: secret except in degenerate low-degree cases.
344: 
345: r[shamir-threshold.information-theoretic-security]
346: Any k - 1 visible shares MUST be completable to any target secret by adding
347: a suitable k-th point at x = 0.
348: 
349: r[shamir-threshold.perfect-reconstruction-threshold]
350: Once the secret point is included, the completed interpolation data MUST
351: fix a unique secret value.
352: 
353: r[consistency-vocab.history-well-formed]
354: A history MUST be well formed when every operation in it is complete under
355: `consistency-vocab.op-complete`.
356: 
357: r[consistency-vocab.realtime-order]
358: Real-time order MUST hold from operation `a` to operation `b` exactly when
359: `a` responds before `b` is invoked.
360: 
361: r[consistency-vocab.session-order]
362: Session order MUST hold from operation `a` to operation `b` exactly when
363: they belong to the same session, have different operation IDs, and `a`
364: completes no later than `b` begins.
365: 
366: r[consistency-vocab.visibility]
367: Visibility MUST hold from a write to a read exactly when the read names
368: that write as its observed source on the same object.
369: 
370: r[consistency-vocab.arbitration]
371: Arbitration MUST give a deterministic order between two writes to the
372: same object by response time, with operation ID as the tie-breaker.
373: 
374: r[consistency-vocab.write-conflict]
375: Two writes MUST conflict exactly when they touch the same object but come
376: from different transactions.
377: 
378: r[consistency-vocab.happens-before]
379: The shared happens-before edge relation MUST be the union of real-time
380: order, session order, and visibility.
381: 
382: ## Transactional Consistency Models
383: 
384: r[consistency-txn.read-uncommitted]
385: Read uncommitted MUST still forbid dirty writes.
386: 
387: r[consistency-txn.read-committed]
388: Read committed MUST extend read uncommitted by forbidding dirty reads.
389: 
390: r[consistency-txn.cursor-stability]
391: Cursor stability MUST extend read committed by protecting cursor-held
392: objects from concurrent modification.
393: 
394: r[consistency-txn.monotonic-atomic-view]
395: Monotonic atomic view MUST extend read committed by requiring all-or-none
396: visibility for effects of already-observed committed transactions.
397: 
398: r[consistency-txn.repeatable-read]
399: Repeatable read MUST extend read committed by keeping rereads of the same
400: object stable within a transaction.
401: 
402: r[consistency-txn.predicate-stability]
403: Predicate stability MUST hold exactly when reevaluating a predicate yields
404: the same membership result.
405: 
406: r[consistency-txn.first-committer-wins]
407: First-committer-wins MUST reject executions in which overlapping snapshots
408: with conflicting write sets both commit.
409: 
410: r[consistency-txn.snapshot-isolation]
411: Snapshot isolation MUST extend read committed with a consistent snapshot,
412: atomic visibility, and first-committer-wins.
413: 
414: r[consistency-txn.serializability]
415: Serializability MUST hold when there exists a serial witness order for the
416: committed transactions.
417: 
418: r[consistency-txn.dependency-acyclic]
419: An acyclic transaction-dependency graph MUST be a valid serializability
420: witness shape.
421: 
422: r[consistency-txn.strict-serializability]
423: Strict serializability MUST extend serializability with real-time and
424: per-session program-order respect across transactions.
425: 
426: ## Object and Session Consistency Models
427: 
428: r[consistency-object.sequential-witness]
429: A sequential witness history MUST be a well-formed total order of complete
430: shared read/write operations expressed with the consistency-history
431: vocabulary.
432: 
433: r[consistency-object.sequential-consistency]
434: Sequential consistency MUST require a shared sequential witness and
435: preserved session/program order.
436: 
437: r[consistency-object.linearizability]
438: Linearizability MUST extend sequential consistency by also preserving
439: shared real-time order.
440: 
441: r[consistency-session.causal-dependency]
442: A reusable causal-dependency witness MUST agree with vector-clock
443: happens-before.
444: 
445: r[consistency-session.causal-ready]
446: Message-level causal readiness MUST reuse the existing causal-delivery
447: readiness rule.
448: 
449: r[consistency-session.read-your-writes]
450: Read-your-writes MUST hold exactly when a session's later reads include
451: its own earlier writes.
452: 
453: r[consistency-session.monotonic-reads]
454: Monotonic reads MUST hold exactly when later reads do not move to an
455: older observed state.
456: 
457: r[consistency-session.monotonic-writes]
458: Monotonic writes MUST hold exactly when same-session writes preserve issue
459: order everywhere.
460: 
461: r[consistency-session.writes-follow-reads]
462: Writes-follow-reads MUST hold exactly when a write after a read is not
463: ordered before the write that produced the read value.
464: 
465: r[consistency-session.pram]
466: PRAM MUST require monotonic reads, monotonic writes, and read-your-writes.
467: 
468: r[consistency-session.causal-consistency]
469: Causal consistency MUST extend PRAM with writes-follow-reads.
470: 
471: ## Consistency Refinement and Availability
472: 
473: r[consistency-refinement.model-hierarchy]
474: The implementation MUST expose proof bridges for the implication edges in
475: the consistency-model hierarchy.
476: 
477: r[consistency-refinement.availability-envelope]
478: The implementation MUST classify each modeled consistency level by the
479: strongest availability envelope assigned in the OpenSpec taxonomy.

481: ## Option Combinators
482: 
483: r[option.unwrap-or-default]
484: unwrap_or_default MUST return the contained value if Some, or the provided
485: default if None.
486: 
487: r[option.map-preserves-none]
488: Mapping over None MUST produce None regardless of the mapping function.
489: Mapping MUST satisfy the functor composition law: map(map(opt, f), g)
490: equals map(opt, g∘f).
491: 
492: r[option.and-then]
493: and_then MUST apply `f` to the contained value if Some, returning its
494: result. and_then on None MUST return None. and_then MUST satisfy the
495: monad identity laws: and_then(Some(v), f) == f(v) and
496: and_then(opt, Some) == opt.
497: 
498: r[option.or-else]
499: or_else MUST return the option unchanged if Some. or_else on None MUST
500: return the fallback value. or_else with a Some fallback MUST always
501: yield Some.
502: 
503: r[option.flatten]
504: flatten on Some(Some(v)) MUST return Some(v). flatten on Some(None) and
505: flatten on None MUST both return None.
506: 
507: r[option.zip]
508: zip MUST return Some((a, b)) if and only if both inputs are Some.
509: If either input is None, zip MUST return None.
510: 
511: r[option.filter]
512: filter MUST return Some(v) when the predicate holds, None when it does
513: not. filter on None MUST return None. filter MUST be idempotent:
514: filter(filter(opt, p), p) == filter(opt, p).
515: 
516: ## Result Combinators
517: 
518: r[result.unwrap-or]
519: unwrap_or MUST return the Ok value if present, or the provided default
520: if Err.
521: 
522: r[result.map-ok]
523: map_ok MUST apply `f` to the Ok value, leaving Err untouched. map_ok
524: MUST satisfy the functor composition law. map_ok and map_err MUST
525: commute: the order of application does not matter.
526: 
527: r[result.map-err]
528: map_err MUST apply `f` to the Err value, leaving Ok untouched.
529: 
530: r[result.and-then]
531: and_then on Ok(v) MUST apply `f`, returning its result. and_then on
532: Err(e) MUST propagate the error unchanged. and_then MUST satisfy the
533: monad right identity: and_then(res, Ok) == res.
534: 
535: r[result.or-else]
536: or_else on Ok(v) MUST return Ok(v) unchanged. or_else on Err MUST return
537: the fallback. or_else with an Ok fallback MUST always yield Ok.
538: 
539: ## Slice
540: 
541: r[slice.chunk-count]
542: chunk_count MUST return the number of full chunks of `chunk_size` that fit
543: in a length of `len`. The result times chunk_size MUST not exceed len. The
544: remainder MUST be less than chunk_size. chunk_size MUST be nonzero.
545: 
546: r[slice.prefix-eq]
547: prefix_eq MUST return true if and only if the first `n` elements of both
548: slices are equal. When n is zero, prefix_eq MUST return true. When n
549: exceeds either slice length, prefix_eq MUST return false.
550: 
551: r[slice.suffix-eq]
552: suffix_eq MUST return true if and only if the last `n` elements of both
553: slices are equal. When n is zero, suffix_eq MUST return true. When n
554: exceeds either slice length, suffix_eq MUST return false.
555: 
556: r[slice.all-equal]
557: all_equal MUST return true if and only if every element in the slice
558: equals the given value. all_equal on an empty slice MUST return true.
559: 
560: r[slice.mismatch-index]
561: mismatch_index MUST return the index of the first position where two
562: slices differ, comparing up to the shorter length. MUST return None if
563: all compared elements match. mismatch_index of two empty slices MUST
564: return None.
565: 
566: ## Conversion
567: 
568: r[conversion.narrow-u32]
569: narrow_u32 MUST return Some when the input fits in u32, None otherwise.
570: Widening a u32 then narrowing MUST return the original value. Values
571: above u32::MAX MUST be rejected.
572: 
573: r[conversion.narrow-u16]
574: narrow_u16 MUST return Some when the input fits in u16, None otherwise.
575: Widening a u16 then narrowing MUST return the original value. Values
576: above u16::MAX MUST be rejected.
577: 
578: r[conversion.narrow-u8]
579: narrow_u8 MUST return Some when the input fits in u8, None otherwise.
580: Widening a u8 then narrowing MUST return the original value. Values
581: above u8::MAX MUST be rejected.
582: 
583: r[conversion.signed-to-unsigned]
584: signed_to_unsigned MUST return Some(x as u64) for non-negative i64
585: values, and None for negative values. The i64 → u64 → i64 roundtrip
586: MUST preserve the value for non-negative inputs.
587: 
588: r[conversion.unsigned-to-signed]
589: unsigned_to_signed MUST return Some(x as i64) when x <= i64::MAX, and
590: None otherwise. The u64 → i64 → u64 roundtrip MUST preserve the value
591: for inputs that fit in i64.

593: ## Expiration
594: 
595: r[expiration.expires-at]
596: expires_at(now_ms, ttl_seconds) MUST return now_ms + ttl_seconds * 1000,
597: saturating at u64::MAX on overflow. The result MUST always be >= now_ms.
598: 
599: r[expiration.is-expired]
600: is_expired(expires_at_ms, now_ms) MUST return true if and only if
601: now_ms > expires_at_ms. At the exact expiration time, the entry is NOT
602: expired.
603: 
604: r[expiration.is-expired-opt]
605: is_expired_opt(expires_at_ms, now_ms) MUST return false when expires_at_ms
606: is None (no TTL means never expires). When Some, MUST delegate to
607: is_expired.
608: 
609: r[expiration.time-remaining]
610: time_remaining(expires_at_ms, now_ms) MUST return None when expires_at_ms
611: is None. MUST return Some(0) when already expired. MUST return
612: Some(expires_at - now) when not yet expired.
613: 
614: r[expiration.is-ttl-valid]
615: is_ttl_valid(ttl_seconds, max_ttl) MUST return true if and only if
616: ttl_seconds <= max_ttl.

618: ## Chain Hash
619: 
620: r[chain.hash-deterministic]
621: The hash function MUST be deterministic: same inputs MUST always produce
622: the same output. Modeled as an uninterpreted function with this axiom.
623: 
624: r[chain.compute-entry-hash]
625: compute_entry_hash MUST combine prev_hash, log_index, term, and data
626: into a single hash input and return the hash. The result MUST depend on
627: all four inputs.
628: 
629: r[chain.chain-valid]
630: A chain is valid if every entry's hash equals the hash computed from its
631: predecessor's hash, its index, its term, and its data. The first entry
632: uses the genesis hash as its predecessor.
633: 
634: r[chain.append-preserves]
635: Appending a correctly-hashed entry to a valid chain MUST produce a valid
636: chain. All prior entries MUST remain valid.
637: 
638: r[chain.collision-free]
639: The hash function MUST be collision-free: if two calls to hash_spec
640: produce the same output, all four inputs MUST be identical. This is an
641: idealized cryptographic assumption (trusted axiom) modeling the
642: collision resistance of Blake3.
643: 
644: r[chain.agreement]
645: If two valid chains have matching hashes at position k, all entries at
646: positions 0 through k MUST be identical. This is the fundamental
647: security guarantee: the hash at any position commits to the entire
648: chain prefix.
649: 
650: r[chain.divergence-detected]
651: If two valid chains differ at any position j, their hashes at every
652: position k >= j MUST differ. Hash chains are tamper-evident: any
653: modification to any entry is detectable by comparing tip hashes.
654: 
655: r[chain.single-entry-valid]
656: A single entry correctly hashed from the genesis hash MUST form a
657: valid chain of length one.
658: 
659: r[chain.tip-commitment]
660: The chain-tip commitment MUST return the genesis hash for an empty chain
661: and the final entry hash for a non-empty chain. For a valid chain, the tip
662: commitment MUST commit to the full prefix under the existing agreement and
663: collision-free assumptions.
664: 
665: r[chain.extension-prefix]
666: A chain extension predicate MUST hold exactly when the shorter chain is an
667: unchanged prefix of the longer chain. Extension MUST remain separate from
668: hash validity, while valid full chains MUST yield valid selected prefixes.
669: 
670: r[chain.checkpoint-anchor]
671: A checkpoint anchor over an index and expected hash MUST be valid only when
672: the chain is valid, the index is in range, and the entry hash at that index
673: matches the expected hash. Matching checkpoint anchors MUST authenticate the
674: prefix through that index.
675: 
676: r[chain.fork-detection]
677: Fork detection MUST identify whether two chains diverge. For valid chains of
678: the same length, equal tip commitments MUST imply no divergence, and any
679: entry divergence MUST force different tip commitments.
680: 
681: r[chain.batch-append]
682: Batch append MUST fold correctly hashed entries over a valid base chain,
683: preserve validity at each append step, and leave the original prefix
684: unchanged. Incorrectly hashed batch entries MUST not receive a verified
685: append-preserves claim.
686: 
687: r[chain.log-shape]
688: Log-shape predicates MUST be separate from hash validity and MUST cover the
689: chosen contiguous/increasing index policy plus term policy. Hash validity
690: alone MUST NOT imply index or term well-formedness.
691: 
692: r[chain.tamper-classification]
693: Tamper-classification lemmas MUST classify detectable valid-chain divergence
694: as data identifier, index, term, or predecessor/hash tampering while reusing
695: existing collision-free, agreement, and divergence facts.
696: 
697: r[chain.domain-separated-hash]
698: Domain-separated hash input contracts MUST distinguish entry, checkpoint,
699: receipt, and snapshot-style commitments. A hash from one domain MUST NOT be
700: accepted as verified evidence for another domain without an explicit
701: compatibility wrapper.
702: 
703: r[chain.runtime-blake3-alignment]
704: Runtime chain hashing MUST either use the documented deterministic BLAKE3
705: serialization boundary or keep any deterministic test-mixer bridge explicit
706: as a trusted/runtime boundary with no cryptographic-strength claim.
707: 
708: r[chain.compact-history-proof]
709: An optional compact-history overlay MAY provide skip-link, Merkle, or MMR
710: membership/range proofs. The overlay MUST compose with base chain tips or
711: checkpoints and MUST NOT replace or weaken linear chain validity.
712: 
713: ## Batch Limits
714: 
715: r[batch.check-limits]
716: check_limits MUST report whether adding an operation would exceed the
717: entry count or byte size limit. An empty batch (zero entries) MUST
718: never report exceeded — the first operation always fits.
719: 
720: r[batch.flush-decision]
721: flush_decision MUST return Immediate when the batch is full (entries or
722: bytes), when batching is disabled (immediate mode), or when the batch
723: is empty. MUST return Delayed when the batch has items but is not full
724: and no flush is already scheduled. MUST return None when a flush is
725: already scheduled.
726: 
727: r[batch.op-size]
728: op_size MUST return key_len + value_len, saturating at u64::MAX.
729: delete_op_size MUST return key_len.
730: 
731: ## Interval
732: 
733: r[interval.contains]
734: contains(lo, hi, x) MUST return true if and only if lo <= x < hi.
735: An empty interval (lo >= hi) MUST contain nothing.
736: 
737: r[interval.is-empty]
738: is_empty(lo, hi) MUST return true if and only if lo >= hi.
739: 
740: r[interval.overlaps]
741: overlaps(a_lo, a_hi, b_lo, b_hi) MUST return true if and only if the
742: intervals share at least one point. Two empty intervals MUST NOT overlap.
743: Overlap MUST be symmetric.
744: 
745: r[interval.split]
746: split(lo, hi, mid) MUST produce two intervals [lo, mid) and [mid, hi)
747: that cover the original without overlap. mid MUST satisfy lo < mid < hi.
748: 
749: r[interval.adjacent]
750: adjacent(a_lo, a_hi, b_lo, b_hi) MUST return true if and only if one
751: interval ends exactly where the other begins. Adjacent MUST be symmetric.
752: 
753: r[interval.merge]
754: merge(a_lo, a_hi, b_lo, b_hi) MUST combine two adjacent intervals into
755: one covering both. Merge of a split MUST recover the original.
756: 
757: ## Compare-and-Swap
758: 
759: r[cas.check-condition]
760: check_condition MUST evaluate a typed condition against a current value:
761: VALUE_EQUALS succeeds when current matches expected, KEY_EXISTS succeeds
762: when current is Some, KEY_NOT_EXISTS succeeds when current is None.
763: Unknown condition types MUST return false.
764: 
765: r[cas.check-cas]
766: check_cas MUST return true if and only if expected and current match:
767: both None, or both Some with equal values. Any other combination MUST
768: return false.
769: 
770: r[cas.evaluate-conditions]
771: evaluate_conditions MUST check conditions in order, returning the index
772: of the first failure. If all conditions pass, MUST return all-met.
773: An empty condition list MUST return all-met.
774: 
775: ## Bitmap
776: 
777: r[bitmap.new]
778: new MUST create a bitmap with num_bits bits, all initially clear. The
779: number of backing u64 words MUST equal ceil(num_bits / 64).
780: 
781: r[bitmap.get]
782: get MUST return true if and only if the bit at the given position is set.
783: Position MUST be less than num_bits.
784: 
785: r[bitmap.set]
786: set MUST set the bit at the given position to 1 without affecting other
787: words. After set, get at the same position MUST return true.
788: 
789: r[bitmap.clear]
790: clear MUST set the bit at the given position to 0 without affecting other
791: words. After clear, get at the same position MUST return false.
792: 
793: r[bitmap.toggle]
794: toggle MUST flip the bit at the given position. Toggling twice MUST
795: restore the original word value.
796: 
797: r[bitmap.len]
798: len MUST return the total number of bits in the bitmap.
799: 
800: r[bitmap.word-count]
801: word_count MUST return the number of u64 words backing the bitmap.
802: 
803: ## Ring Buffer
804: 
805: r[ring-buffer.new]
806: new MUST create an empty ring buffer with the given power-of-two capacity.
807: The result MUST satisfy the well-formedness invariant with count zero.
808: 
809: r[ring-buffer.push]
810: push MUST write the value at the tail position and advance the tail
811: with wraparound. push MUST return true on success and false when full.
812: Count MUST increase by one on success. The buffer MUST remain well-formed.
813: 
814: r[ring-buffer.pop]
815: pop MUST return Some with the head element and advance the head with
816: wraparound. pop MUST return None when empty. Count MUST decrease by one
817: on success. The buffer MUST remain well-formed.
818: 
819: r[ring-buffer.peek]
820: peek MUST return Some with the head element without modifying the buffer.
821: peek MUST return None when empty.
822: 
823: r[ring-buffer.len]
824: len MUST return the current count of elements.
825: 
826: r[ring-buffer.is-empty]
827: is_empty MUST return true if and only if count is zero. An empty buffer
828: with nonzero capacity MUST NOT be full.
829: 
830: r[ring-buffer.is-full]
831: is_full MUST return true if and only if count equals capacity.
832: 
833: r[ring-buffer.capacity]
834: capacity MUST return the buffer's fixed capacity.
835: 
836: r[ring-buffer.remaining]
837: remaining MUST return capacity minus current count. remaining plus len
838: MUST equal capacity.
839: 
840: r[ring-buffer.full-batches]
841: full_batches MUST return the number of complete batches of the given
842: size that can be popped from the current contents.
843: 
844: ## Quorum
845: 
846: r[quorum.majority]
847: majority(n) MUST return n / 2 + 1 for any n > 0. majority(1) MUST be 1.
848: majority(2) MUST be 2. majority(5) MUST be 3. The result MUST satisfy
849: 1 <= majority(n) <= n.
850: 
851: r[quorum.is-quorum]
852: is_quorum(count, total) MUST return true if and only if count >=
853: majority(total). total MUST be greater than zero.
854: 
855: r[quorum.intersection]
856: If is_quorum(a, n) and is_quorum(b, n) both hold, then a + b MUST be
857: greater than n. Two quorums of the same set MUST always overlap.
858: 
859: r[quorum.fault-tolerance]
860: fault_tolerance(n) MUST return (n - 1) / 2 for n > 0, and 0 for n == 0.
861: This is the maximum number of node failures a cluster of size n can
862: tolerate while maintaining quorum.
863: 
864: r[quorum.can-remove-safely]
865: can_remove_safely(n) MUST return true if and only if removing one voter
866: from a cluster of n still leaves a quorum. MUST return false for n <= 2
867: and true for n >= 3.
868: 
869: r[quorum.min-cluster-size]
870: min_cluster_size(f) MUST return 2*f + 1 — the smallest cluster that
871: tolerates f failures. min_cluster_size(fault_tolerance(n)) MUST be <= n
872: for all n > 0.
873: 
874: ## Monotonic
875: 
876: r[monotonic.is-advance]
877: is_advance(old, new) MUST return true if and only if new >= old. Advance
878: MUST be reflexive, transitive, and antisymmetric.
879: 
880: r[monotonic.is-strict-advance]
881: is_strict_advance(old, new) MUST return true if and only if new > old.
882: Strict advance MUST be irreflexive and transitive. A strict advance
883: followed by a non-strict advance MUST still be a strict advance.
884: 
885: ## Epoch
886: 
887: r[epoch.cmp]
888: epoch_cmp MUST compare (term, index) pairs lexicographically: first by
889: term, then by index. MUST return -1 if a < b, 0 if a == b, 1 if a > b.
890: The ordering MUST be total, transitive, and antisymmetric.
891: 
892: r[epoch.ge]
893: epoch_ge(a, b) MUST return true if and only if epoch a is greater than
894: or equal to b in the lexicographic ordering. This is the vote-granting
895: predicate: a candidate's log must be at least as up-to-date as the voter's.
896: 
897: ## ACID Transaction Properties
898: 
899: r[acid.apply-write]
900: apply_write MUST update the state at the given index to the new value,
901: leaving all other positions unchanged. The state length MUST be preserved.
902: All write indices MUST be within state bounds.
903: 
904: r[acid.commit]
905: commit (apply_writes) MUST apply all write operations in sequence.
906: Committing an empty write set MUST return the state unchanged. The
907: state length MUST be preserved after commit.
908: 
909: r[acid.abort]
910: abort MUST return the state unchanged. No positions are modified.
911: 
912: r[acid.atomicity]
913: A committed transaction MUST have all writes applied — the final state
914: reflects every write in order. An aborted transaction MUST leave the
915: state identical to the original. The state length MUST be preserved.
916: No partial application is possible.
917: 
918: r[acid.consistency]
919: Positions not targeted by any write operation MUST retain their original
920: values after commit. Only explicitly written positions may change.
921: 
922: r[acid.isolation]
923: Two writes to distinct positions MUST commute: applying write A then B
924: MUST produce the same state as applying B then A when their indices
925: differ. Reading a position not targeted by a write MUST return the
926: original value.
927: 
928: r[acid.durability]
929: WAL recovery MUST replay all committed entries and skip uncommitted
930: entries. Recovering a fully committed WAL MUST produce the same state
931: as a direct commit. Recovering a fully uncommitted WAL MUST leave
932: the state unchanged. Recovery MUST preserve state length.
933: 
934: r[acid.writes-disjoint]
935: writes_disjoint MUST return true if and only if no write index in the
936: first set matches any write index in the second set.
937: 
938: ## Copy-on-Write
939: 
940: r[cow.should-copy]
941: should_copy(ref_count) MUST return true if and only if ref_count > 1.
942: An exclusive owner (ref_count == 1) MUST NOT require a copy.
943: 
944: r[cow.ref-count-after-clone]
945: ref_count_after_clone MUST return ref_count + 1, saturating at u64::MAX.
946: The result MUST always be greater than or equal to the input.
947: 
948: r[cow.ref-count-after-drop]
949: ref_count_after_drop MUST return ref_count - 1 when ref_count > 0, and
950: 0 when ref_count is already 0. The result MUST always be less than or
951: equal to the input.
952: 
953: r[cow.is-exclusive]
954: is_exclusive MUST return true if and only if ref_count == 1. Exclusive
955: ownership and should_copy MUST be complements for any valid (> 0) ref
956: count.
957: 
958: r[cow.can-reclaim]
959: can_reclaim MUST return true if and only if ref_count == 0. Storage
960: backing a COW value MUST only be freed when no references remain.
961: 
962: r[cow.snapshot-isolation]
963: After a COW write on shared data, readers MUST see the old value and
964: the writer MUST see the new value. When exclusive, the writer sees the
965: new value and no other readers exist.
966: 
967: ## Approval
968: 
969: r[approval.count-valid]
970: count_valid_approvals MUST return the number of entries where both
971: approved and matches_head_commit are true. The count MUST be less than
972: or equal to the total length. An empty input MUST yield zero.
973: 
974: r[approval.is-merge-allowed]
975: is_merge_allowed MUST return true if and only if ci_passed is true AND
976: valid_count >= required. If CI has not passed, merge MUST NOT be allowed
977: regardless of approval count.
978: 
979: r[approval.needs-more]
980: needs_more_approvals MUST return required - valid_count when valid_count
981: < required, and zero otherwise. The result MUST be zero if and only if
982: valid_count >= required.
983: 
984: r[approval.has-stale]
985: has_stale_approvals MUST return true if any entry has approved true but
986: matches_head_commit false. An empty input MUST return false.
987: 
988: ## Bounded Range
989: 
990: r[bounded-range.contains]
991: contains MUST return true if x >= lower and either the range is unbounded
992: or x < upper. An unbounded range MUST contain all x >= lower. An empty
993: bounded range MUST contain nothing.
994: 
995: r[bounded-range.is-empty]
996: is_empty MUST return true if and only if the range is bounded and
997: lower >= upper. Unbounded ranges MUST never be empty.
998: 
999: r[bounded-range.overlaps]
1000: overlaps MUST return true if and only if two non-empty ranges share at
1001: least one point. Overlap MUST be symmetric. Empty ranges MUST NOT
1002: overlap. Two non-empty unbounded ranges MUST always overlap.
1003: 
1004: r[bounded-range.is-bounded]
1005: is_bounded MUST return true if and only if has_upper is true and
1006: lower < upper. Bounded implies non-empty.
1007: 
1008: r[bounded-range.restrict]
1009: restrict MUST produce a bounded range with the same lower bound and an
1010: upper bound of new_upper (or min of current and new_upper for already-
1011: bounded ranges). The result MUST be a subset of the input range.
1012: 
1013: ## Chunk
1014: 
1015: r[chunk.count-ceil]
1016: chunk_count_ceil MUST return the number of chunks needed including a
1017: partial last chunk. MUST use ceiling division without overflow:
1018: if total_size == 0 then 0, else (total_size - 1) / chunk_size + 1.
1019: chunk_size MUST be nonzero.
1020: 
1021: r[chunk.size-at]
1022: chunk_size_at MUST return the size of the chunk at the given index. All
1023: chunks except possibly the last MUST have size chunk_size. The last chunk
1024: MUST have size total_size - index * chunk_size. The result MUST be > 0
1025: and <= chunk_size. index MUST be < chunk_count_ceil.
1026: 
1027: r[chunk.offset]
1028: chunk_offset MUST return index * chunk_size. The multiplication MUST
1029: NOT overflow. chunk_size MUST be nonzero.
1030: 
1031: r[chunk.index-for-offset]
1032: chunk_index_for_offset MUST return offset / chunk_size. chunk_size MUST
1033: be nonzero.
1034: 
1035: r[chunk.offset-within]
1036: offset_within_chunk MUST return offset % chunk_size. The result MUST be
1037: less than chunk_size. chunk_size MUST be nonzero.
1038: 
1039: ## Drain
1040: 
1041: r[drain.can-start-op]
1042: can_start_op MUST return true if and only if is_draining is false. New
1043: operations MUST NOT be admitted during drain.
1044: 
1045: r[drain.after-start-op]
1046: after_start_op MUST return in_flight + 1. in_flight MUST be less than
1047: u64::MAX to prevent overflow.
1048: 
1049: r[drain.after-finish-op]
1050: after_finish_op MUST return in_flight - 1. in_flight MUST be greater
1051: than zero to prevent underflow.
1052: 
1053: r[drain.is-drain-complete]
1054: is_drain_complete MUST return true if and only if is_draining is true
1055: AND in_flight is zero. Both conditions MUST hold.
1056: 
1057: r[drain.should-notify]
1058: should_notify MUST return true if and only if is_draining is true,
1059: old_in_flight > 0, and new_in_flight == 0. This detects the transition
1060: when the last operation finishes during drain.
1061: 
1062: r[drain.start-drain]
1063: start_drain_decision MUST return 0 if already draining, 1 if drain
1064: completes immediately (no in-flight ops), 2 if drain starts but must
1065: wait. The result MUST always be 0, 1, or 2.
1066: 
1067: ## Cache Partitioning
1068: 
1069: r[cache-partition.isolation]
1070: A lookup for partition P MUST NOT hit a line stored in a way assigned to
1071: partition Q (Q ≠ P). lookup_partitioned MUST only examine ways assigned
1072: to the requesting partition.
1073: 
1074: r[cache-partition.eviction-containment]
1075: Eviction within partition P MUST only select victim ways assigned to P.
1076: Lines in other partitions MUST be untouched by the eviction.
1077: 
1078: r[cache-partition.capacity]
1079: The sum of all partition sizes (in ways) MUST equal the total number of
1080: ways. No capacity is lost or double-counted at partition boundaries.
1081: 
1082: r[cache-partition.assignment]
1083: Every way MUST be assigned to exactly one valid partition. A valid
1084: assignment maps every way to a partition ID in [0, num_partitions).
1085: 
1086: r[cache-partition.resize]
1087: Resizing a partition MUST invalidate transferred ways before
1088: reassignment. Non-transferred ways MUST remain unchanged in both
1089: assignment and data. Total capacity MUST be preserved.
1090: 
1091: r[cache-partition.full-equivalence]
1092: A single partition containing all ways MUST behave identically to an
1093: unpartitioned cache: lookup examines all ways and eviction considers
1094: all ways.
1095: 
1096: ## Eviction
1097: 
1098: r[eviction.should-evict]
1099: should_evict MUST return true if and only if count >= capacity. The
1100: cache is at or over capacity and eviction is needed.
1101: 
1102: r[eviction.find-lru]
1103: find_lru_candidate MUST return the index of the entry with the smallest
1104: access_time among non-protected entries. MUST return None if all entries
1105: are protected or the slice is empty. When found, the entry at the
1106: returned index MUST NOT be protected and MUST have access_time <= all
1107: other non-protected entries.
1108: 
1109: r[eviction.cache-valid]
1110: is_cache_valid MUST return true if and only if count <= capacity + 1
1111: AND protected_count <= count. The cache may temporarily exceed capacity
1112: by one before eviction runs.
1113: 
1114: r[eviction.evictable-count]
1115: evictable_count MUST return count - protected_count using saturating
1116: subtraction. The result MUST be <= count.
1117: 
1118: ## Set-Associative Lookup
1119: 
1120: r[set-assoc.decomposition]
1121: Decomposing an address into tag, index, and offset MUST preserve all
1122: information needed to reconstruct the original address. For any valid
1123: `offset_bits` and `index_bits` with `offset_bits + index_bits <= 64`,
1124: `reconstruct_address(decompose_address(addr))` MUST equal `addr`.
1125: 
1126: r[set-assoc.component-bounds]
1127: extract_offset MUST return a value that fits in `offset_bits` bits.
1128: extract_index MUST return a value that fits in `index_bits` bits.
1129: extract_tag MUST return a value that fits in the remaining
1130: `64 - offset_bits - index_bits` tag bits.
1131: 
1132: r[set-assoc.hit]
1133: find_way(set, tag) MUST return `Some(i)` only when `set[i] == Some(tag)`.
1134: lookup_set(set, addr, offset_bits, index_bits) MUST return the way whose
1135: stored tag matches `extract_tag(addr, offset_bits, index_bits)`.
1136: 
1137: r[set-assoc.miss]
1138: find_way(set, tag) MUST return `None` only when no way in the set holds
1139: `Some(tag)`. lookup_set MUST miss when every way disagrees with the
1140: requested tag.
1141: 
1142: r[set-assoc.no-duplicates]
1143: Within a set, at most one way SHOULD hold a given non-empty tag.
1144: check_no_duplicate_tags MUST return true if and only if no two distinct
1145: ways hold the same `Some(tag)` value.
1146: 
1147: r[set-assoc.insert-preserves-uniqueness]
1148: Inserting a tag into an empty way of a set that already has no duplicate
1149: tags, when that tag is absent from all other ways, MUST preserve the
1150: no-duplicate-tags invariant.
1151: 
1152: r[set-assoc.no-aliasing]
1153: For two addresses with the same index but different tags, a hit for one
1154: MUST NOT be a hit for the other's tag. The matched way MUST identify the
1155: requested line, not another tag that shares the set.
1156: 
1157: r[set-assoc.set-isolation]
1158: Changing a cache set whose index differs from the requested address's
1159: index MUST NOT change the lookup result for that address. Different
1160: indices MUST select different sets.
1161: 
1162: ## False Sharing Detection
1163: 
1164: r[false-sharing.same-line]
1165: same_cache_line MUST return true if and only if the two addresses are in
1166: the same cache line. For power-of-two `line_size`, this is equivalent to
1167: comparing the address bits above the offset.
1168: 
1169: r[false-sharing.distinct-line]
1170: If two addresses are on different cache lines, they MUST NOT false-share.
1171: For canonical tag/index decomposition, this means at least one of tag or
1172: index differs.
1173: 
1174: r[false-sharing.alignment]
1175: is_line_aligned MUST return true if and only if `addr % line_size == 0`.
1176: line_start MUST clear the offset bits and return the first byte address of
1177: the containing line.
1178: 
1179: r[false-sharing.padding]
1180: padding_prevents_sharing(addr_a, size_a, addr_b, line_size) MUST return
1181: true if and only if object B starts at least one full cache line after the
1182: end of object A: `addr_b >= addr_a + size_a + line_size`. Under that
1183: condition, no byte of A may share a cache line with any byte at or after
1184: `addr_b`.
1185: 
1186: r[false-sharing.object-span]
1187: cache_lines_spanned MUST return the number of cache lines touched by a
1188: positive-size object, equal to `ceil((addr % line_size + size) /
1189: line_size)`. For this computation, `(addr % line_size) + size` MUST fit
1190: in `u64`.
1191: 
1192: r[false-sharing.decomposition-equivalence]
1193: For `offset_bits < 64` and `offset_bits + index_bits <= 64`,
1194: same_cache_line(a, b, 1 << offset_bits) MUST be equivalent to
1195: `extract_tag(a, offset_bits, index_bits) == extract_tag(b, offset_bits,
1196: index_bits)` and `extract_index(a, offset_bits, index_bits) ==
1197: extract_index(b, offset_bits, index_bits)`.
1198: 
1199: ## Write Policy
1200: 
1201: r[write-policy.write-back-dirty]
1202: Under write-back policy, a store MUST set the dirty bit and a freshly
1203: loaded line MUST be clean.
1204: 
1205: r[write-policy.write-back-eviction]
1206: Evicting a dirty line MUST write its data to memory at the selected
1207: address. Evicting a clean line MUST leave memory unchanged.
1208: 
1209: r[write-policy.write-through-clean]
1210: Under write-through policy, stores and loads MUST leave the dirty bit
1211: clear.
1212: 
1213: r[write-policy.write-through-memory]
1214: A write-through store MUST update memory immediately at the selected
1215: address, and the updated memory cell MUST equal the cache line's new data.
1216: 
1217: r[write-policy.policy-non-interference]
1218: Updating one cache line in a mixed-policy cache MUST NOT change any other
1219: line's state.
1220: 
1221: r[write-policy.flush-all]
1222: When every clean line already matches memory, flush_all MUST clear every
1223: line's dirty bit and leave memory matching every cache line's data.
1224: 
1225: r[write-policy.read-equivalence]
1226: A read hit MUST return the cached data regardless of whether the line uses
1227: write-back or write-through policy.
1228: 
1229: ## MOESI Coherence
1230: 
1231: r[moesi.single-writer]
1232: At most one cache MAY hold a line in a dirty-owner state (`Modified` or
1233: `Owned`) at a time.
1234: 
1235: r[moesi.owned-entry]
1236: A remote read against a `Modified` owner MUST move that owner to
1237: `Owned` while the requester receives a shared copy.
1238: 
1239: r[moesi.owned-supply]
1240: When any cache holds a line in `Owned`, reads MUST source dirty data from
1241: some cache rather than from memory.
1242: 
1243: r[moesi.writeback]
1244: Evicting an `Owned` line MUST write back to memory before the owner is
1245: lost. Evicting a `Shared` line MUST NOT require a writeback.
1246: 
1247: r[moesi.transitions]
1248: Every valid processor event and snoop bus action MUST produce a valid
1249: next state and a valid bus action/result.
1250: 
1251: r[moesi.mesi-refinement]
1252: For transitions that stay within the `M/E/S/I` subset, MOESI MUST agree
1253: with the existing MESI transition model after mapping `Owned -> Shared`.
1254: 
1255: r[moesi.no-stale-reads]
1256: Under the memory-consistency relation `memory_up_to_date <==>
1257: !dirty_owner_exists`, reads MUST use memory only when memory is current;
1258: otherwise some cache MUST be the read source.
1259: 
1260: ## Cache Hierarchy
1261: 
1262: Cache hierarchy levels are modeled as canonical finite sets of line tags.
1263: Exec code may represent a level as a deduplicated sequence, but the
1264: requirements below are about line presence and absence.
1265: 
1266: r[hierarchy.inclusive-invariant]
1267: Under the inclusive policy, every line present in L1 MUST also be present
1268: in L2 after every modeled operation.
1269: 
1270: r[hierarchy.back-invalidation]
1271: Under the inclusive policy, evicting a line from L2 MUST also invalidate
1272: that line from L1 so the inclusive invariant is preserved.
1273: 
1274: r[hierarchy.exclusive-invariant]
1275: Under the exclusive policy, no line may be present in both L1 and L2 at
1276: the same time.
1277: 
1278: r[hierarchy.exclusive-swap]
1279: Under the exclusive policy, promoting a line from L2 to L1 MUST remove it
1280: from L2 in the same abstract step.
1281: 
1282: r[hierarchy.non-inclusive]
1283: Under the non-inclusive policy, the hierarchy MUST impose no subset or
1284: disjointness constraint between L1 and L2.
1285: 
1286: r[hierarchy.capacity]
1287: For canonical levels, the inclusive effective capacity MUST equal |L2|,
1288: and the exclusive effective capacity MUST equal |L1| + |L2|.
1289: 
1290: r[hierarchy.snoop-scope]
1291: Under the inclusive policy, an L2 miss MUST imply an L1 miss for the same
1292: line. Under the exclusive policy, checking L2 alone MUST NOT be assumed
1293: sufficient.
1294: 
1295: ## Store Buffer Forwarding
1296: 
1297: r[store-buffer.youngest-match]
1298: When more than one buffered store can satisfy a load, forwarding MUST
1299: select the youngest matching store.
1300: 
1301: r[store-buffer.full-coverage]
1302: A load MUST forward from a buffered store only when that store fully
1303: covers the load byte range.
1304: 
1305: r[store-buffer.cache-fallback]
1306: When no buffered store matches a load, the load MUST use the cache path
1307: instead of forwarding.
1308: 
1309: r[store-buffer.drain-ordering]
1310: Buffered stores MUST drain in FIFO order: the oldest store commits first,
1311: and draining one store MUST preserve the relative order of the remaining
1312: stores.
1313: 
1314: r[store-buffer.fence]
1315: A store fence MUST leave the buffer empty before any post-fence store is
1316: enqueued.
1317: 
1318: r[store-buffer.capacity]
1319: When the store buffer is full, enqueue MUST reject the new store rather
1320: than silently dropping it. When the buffer is not full, enqueue MUST grow
1321: the buffer by exactly one entry.
1322: 
1323: ## Cache Prefetch
1324: 
1325: r[cache-prefetch.no-fault]
1326: Prefetching an invalid or inaccessible address MUST be a no-op for the
1327: modeled cache state and MUST NOT modify architectural state.
1328: 
1329: r[cache-prefetch.invisible]
1330: Prefetch operations MUST leave registers, memory contents, and the program
1331: counter unchanged. Prefetch only affects modeled cache state.
1332: 
1333: r[cache-prefetch.cache-effect]
1334: A valid prefetch-for-read MUST leave the requester in a valid MESI state
1335: matching a demand read miss, and a valid prefetch-for-write MUST leave the
1336: requester in Exclusive while invalidating other modeled holders.
1337: 
1338: r[cache-prefetch.coherence]
1339: A valid prefetch-for-read MUST issue BusRead and a valid prefetch-for-write
1340: MUST issue BusReadX. Invalid-address prefetches MUST issue no bus action.
1341: 
1342: r[cache-prefetch.drop-safe]
1343: Dropping a modeled prefetch step MUST leave both architectural state and
1344: cache state unchanged.
1345: 
1346: r[cache-prefetch.eviction-safe]
1347: Replacing a prefetched line MUST write back a dirty victim to memory before
1348: installation. Replacing a clean victim MUST leave memory unchanged.
1349: 
1350: ## Directory Coherence
1351: 
1352: r[directory.consistency]
1353: The directory's owner and sharer bit-vector MUST agree with the actual MESI
1354: state held by each modeled cache at all times.
1355: 
1356: r[directory.invalidation]
1357: Granting a write request MUST emit targeted invalidations to every other cache
1358: that currently holds the line, and the post-ack state MUST leave those caches
1359: invalid.
1360: 
1361: r[directory.single-writer]
1362: A completed write grant MUST leave exactly one modeled cache with the line in
1363: Modified and every other cache Invalid.
1364: 
1365: r[directory.eviction-notify]
1366: Evicting a tracked line MUST clear the corresponding owner or sharer record. A
1367: Modified owner eviction MUST request writeback before the line becomes uncached.
